questions.question: A can complete a work in 20 days, while B can complete the same work in 25 days. Both worked together for 10 days and then C alone completed the remaining work in 10 days. In how many days will A, B and C together complete the same work?
questions.solution:
Given: 

A can complete a work in 20 days.

B can complete the same work in 25 days.

Both worked together for 10 days and then C alone completed the remaining work in 10 days.

Concept used:

Entire work = Work done each day × Time taken to finish the entire work 

Calculation:

LCM (20, 25) = 100

Let the entire work be given by the LCM of the time taken by A & B.

So, the entire work = 100 units

Now,

A does each day = 100 ÷ 20 = 5 units

B does each day = 100 ÷ 25 = 4 units

So, in 10 days A and B together do = (5 + 4) × 10 = 90 units

Remaining work = (100 - 90) = 10 units

So, C does each day = (10 ÷ 10) = 1 unit

Then, A, B and C together do each day = (5 + 4 + 1) = 10 units

So, the time is taken by them to finish the work together = (100 ÷ 10) = 10 days

**∴ In 10 days A, B and C together will complete the same work.**

questions.question: A can do a piece of work in 10 days. B can do it in 15 days. With the assistance of C they completed the work in 5 days. Find in how many days C alone can do it?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A can do a piece of work in 10 days.

B can do it in 15 days. 

With the assistance of C, they completed the work in 5 days

**Formula Used:**

Total work = Efficiency x Time taken

**Calculations:**

⇒ A can-do work = 10 days

⇒ B can do the work = 15 days

⇒ A + B + C can do the work = 5 days

For total work

⇒ Total work = LCM of (10, 15, 5) = 30

⇒ Efficiency of A = Total Work / Time taken = 30/10 = 3 unit

⇒ Efficiency of B = Total Work / Time taken = 30/15 = 2 unit

⇒ Efficiency of A + B + C= Total Work / Time taken = 30/5 = 6 unit

⇒ The efficiency of C = Efficiency of A + B + C - Efficiency of A - Efficiency of B = 6 - 3 - 2 = 1

Time taken by C to do the work alone

⇒ Time taken = Total Work/Efficiency = 30/1 = 30 days

⇒ **Hence, C can do the work alone in 30 days.**

Concept used:

Total work = Number of workers × Efficiency of each worker × Number of days required

Let the efficiency of each man be M.

Total work = 450 × M × 20 = 9000M

Now, the number of men required to complete the task in 30 days = 9000M ÷ (M × 30) = 300

∴ 300 men can finish the construction in 30 days.

questions.question: A and B can complete a work in 36 days and 45 days respectively. They worked together for 2 days and then A left the work. In how many days will B complete the remaining work?

questions.question: Ali, Avtar Singh and Ashok working together can finish a work in 8 days. Ali alone can do it in 20 days and Avtar Singh alone can do it in 24 days. In how many days can Ashok alone do the same work?
questions.solution:
**Given**

**Concept used

Work = Time × Efficiency

Calculation**

Total work = LCM of 8, 20 and 24 = 120 units

Total efficiency = 120/8 = 15 unit/day

Ali's efficiency = 120/20 = 6 unit/day

Avtar's efficiency = 120/24 = 5 unit/day

questions.question: A and B can do a piece of work in eight days and B alone can do it in 16 days. In how many days, can A do it alone?

**Given:**

A and B can do a piece of work in 8 days.

**Formula Used:**

Work done by A and B together in one day = 1/8

Work done by B alone in one day = 1/16

Work done by A alone in one day = (Work done by A and B together in one day) - (Work done by B alone in one day)

Number of days A alone can do the work = 1 / (Work done by A alone in one day)

**Calculation:**

Work done by A and B together in one day = 1/8

Work done by B alone in one day = 1/16

Work done by A alone in one day = (1/8) - (1/16)

⇒ Work done by A alone in one day = (2/16) - (1/16)

⇒ Work done by A alone in one day = 1/16

Number of days A alone can do the work = 1 / (1/16)

⇒ Number of days A alone can do the work = 16

**The correct answer is option 3: 16 days.**

Total Work = Efficiency x Time taken

Amount per day = Total amount/Efficiency of both

⇒ Efficiency of A = Total work / Time taken = 30 / 10 = 3 unit work in one day

⇒ Efficiency of B = Total work / Time taken = 30 / 15 = 2 unit work in one day

⇒ The efficiency of both = Efficiency of A + Efficiency of B = 3 + 2 = 5

⇒ Amount per day = Total amount / Efficiency of both = 1250 / 5 = Rs. 250

⇒ The amount B get = Amount per day x Efficiency of B = 250 x 2 = Rs. 500

**⇒ Hence, The share of B is Rs. 500.**
